newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends higher, propelled by cold.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends higher, propelled by cold.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures surged higher on Monday with gains inspired by forecasts of cold weather on both sides of the Atlantic, brokers said.
Feb Brent closed 45 cents up at $24.57 a barrel, off the session high of $24.73 as dealers locked in profits shortly before the close.
"It's been really strong, basically on the back of (NYMEX) heating oil which has pushed everything else up," said one broker.
"We saw a bit of profit-taking towards the end but that's what you'd expect on a day like this," he said.
U.S. heating oil galloped higher, leading up the whole complex, after forecasters predicted another cold snap in the key Northeastern U.S. market.

Independent weather forecaster Weather Services Corp said European temperatures would remain below normal until Thursday, while in the U.S. Northeast temperatures would dip below normal after a mild spell.
Brokers also said that large investment funds were switching capital into the oil markets.
"There's definitely been good fund buying in the States," said one.
January gas oil ended up a hefty $4.50 a tonne at $232, although February fared better gaining $5.75 on the day. The front month backwardation shed $1.25 on the day to close at $3.25 a tonne.
"The whole market has come up because heating oil has been very strong this afternoon," said one broker. "But a lot of the (gas oil) volume going through has been on the spread."
The Jan/Feb spread came under pressure as dealers rolled forward long positions ahead of the January contract's expiry on Friday.
Europe's physical gas oil markets were also strong as the rally in U.S. heating oil prices closed an arbitrage play from the U.S. Gulf to northwest Europe.
